document_summary: LAHD's RSO Overview page for Los Angeles, CA, explaining which rental properties fall under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, allowable rent increases, registration, eviction grounds and relocation assistance.

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) allowable rent increases
rules.requirement: Rent on RSO units may be increased only once every 12 months by the annual allowable rent increase percentage. Effective February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add a utilities percentage, and the extra 10% for an added dependent is no longer permitted (10% for an additional non-dependent tenant is still allowed).
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage (percentage is in a linked PDF, not in this text); no utilities add-on since 2026-02-02
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28; includes apartments, duplexes, condominiums and townhomes, ADUs and JADUs, and rooms in hotels or rooming houses occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days. Mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks are also covered.
rules.exemptions: Rent amount is not regulated for condominium and townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Luxury exemption available if the monthly rent charged on or before May 31, 1978 can be established. Rent may go to market rate after voluntary move-out, certain at-fault evictions, or a Tenant Buyout Agreement.
rules.interaction: Citywide local rent stabilization. The state Tenant Protection Act cap does not apply to units already covered by local rent control.
rules.citation: L.A.M.C. ch. XV, art. 1, § 151.00 et seq. (Rent Stabilization Ordinance)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: the new RSO formula has two published effective dates, 2026-02-02 per LAHD and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association. This LAHD page gives February 2, 2026; the landlord-association date is not found in this capture.
rules.extraction_notes: The effective date is for the 2026 change (utility add-on removed, dependent 10% removed). The numeric allowable percentage is in a linked PDF not captured here. The page also lists surcharges, registration fees and approved-increase programs (capital improvement, primary renovation, etc.), not extracted separately. Source is LAHD summary page, last modified 2026-09-22.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenancies may be ended only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD, written notice, and payment of tenant relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Eviction only for listed at-fault or no-fault grounds; relocation assistance required for no-fault evictions (amounts not stated in this document)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance; non-RSO units remain covered by the City's Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.interaction: Non-RSO rental units are covered by the separate Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance. All RSO termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.quoted_span:
No-fault evictions require the payment of
relocation assistance
rules.extraction_notes: No effective date is stated in this document. No-fault grounds listed: owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition or permanent removal from the rental market, government order, and conversion to affordable housing. A Notice of Right to Counsel is required beginning August 20, 2025. Relocation amounts are not given on this page.
